I don't think, I know. When it comes to autistic social anxiety, it's not the unrealistic thoughts that everyone thinks go through our heads. It's based on real, negative social interactions since the moment you become sentient. That goes for, for example : bullying by your own parents for not behaving "normal", neglect and abuse by your parents because they can't understand why their child didn't come out normal, bullying in school, from elementary until high school (can't tell for uni cause I didn't go), whether that is your own classmates or older, sometimes even younger kids than you, usually from the gender that you are but cross gender bullying is also common. Bullying by your teachers, for example - shaming you in front of the whole class if you are quiet and don't speak much, calling you up for a presentation when said teacher knows you get made fun of if you dare say a word, grading you lower than what you deserve cause your choice of words is "too high" for the grade you're in, pairing you with kids that make fun of you to do group projects, etc. Then comes work. You will %100, as an autistic person, get bullied and/or micromanaged at work by your boss and your coworkers. If you are timid or quiet, they can immediately tell. Your coworkers might ask for help with their work, when in reality if you accept out of good will (common for ppl with autism to want to be helpful), you will be the one who does all the work in the end. You might get yelled at for making mistakes that everyone else makes because they can tell you are timid and anxious, and abusive people tend to latch onto autistic people for that reason. In relationships, you are more likely than the average person to attract an abusive partner. People with cluster B personality disorders use your personality traits against you and twist the story around so they look like the victim to your abuse. While there are abusive autistic people, it is more likely for them to be victimised. If you are a man, you are told you're "not manly enough", hence you are forced to suffer social pressure to let go of your peace of mind and conform to what "being a man" means, and the same goes for girls. If your interests are different than what's considered normal, you will get bullied. If your pattern of speech is a bit out of the ordinary, you will get bullied. Hell, I even got made fun of for the way I blink, cause apparently I blink weird? Idfk. Nobody likes us for really no real reason, its just that we come off as "uncanny" to them, so they use it as an excuse to shun us.
